numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For float16 input with many elements (e.g. 65521 or 50001 elements), np.quantile/np.percentile return inaccurate results (index calculation overflows float16 precision). Example: np.quantile(np.arange(50_001, dtype=np.float16), .999) returns 49920.0. For arr=np.zeros(65521, dtype=np.float16) with arr[:10]=1 and q=50, several methods return nan (interpolated_inverted_cdf, hazen, weibull, linear, median_unbiased, normal_unbiased), while inverted_cdf returns 0.0, averaged_inverted_cdf returns 1.0, closest_observation returns 0.0. Also, np.percentile(np.ones(10, dtype='float32'), np.float64(3)) does not return float64 as the q dtype should ensure.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: np.quantile(np.arange(50_001, dtype=np.float16), .999) should return 49950.0. The float16 percentile results should be accurate, computed with higher-precision intermediates while keeping float16 output type for float16 input. The float64 q dtype should produce a float64 result type for np.percentile(np.ones(10, dtype='float32'), np.float64(3)).
trigger_conditions: input dtype float16 with large number of elements (around 50001 to 65521)
index calculation performed in float16 precision
methods such as linear, hazen, weibull, median_unbiased, normal_unbiased, interpolated_inverted_cdf for the zeros-with-ones array case
q given as np.float64 while data is float32 (return type issue from issue 30586)
